premises: The actual parsed occurrence is a quality predicate, not a measure/quantity modifier, noun, interjection, or degree-only construction.
A semantic-domain qualifier has an independently verified native meaning restricting evaluation to moral principles and is structurally bound to this quality head.
The quality meaning in this qualified frame corresponds to one of the independently signed native moral-quality meanings above, with the exact canonical evaluation pole retained as provenance.
The contextual result records this frame assumption, the source identities, modifier/head positions and all surviving finer identity alternatives.
conditional_derivation.conclusion: Within that explicitly licensed qualified frame, the quality occurrence has GOOD=+1 for the positive evaluation pole or GOOD=-1 for the negative evaluation pole. This is an additional contextual constraint, not selection of an unqualified fine dictionary ID.
conditional_derivation.identity_policy: Generic quality identities may remain open and survive under this contextual constraint. Their unqualified stored banks are not rewritten; finer identity uncertainty does not itself invalidate a justified frame-conditioned scalar consequence.
conditional_derivation.failure_policy: If attachment, domain interpretation or quality-pole correspondence is not established, retain an unresolved/conditional alternative rather than asserting an unconditional sign or deleting a rival.
